messages.content: Write the invitation copy for a webinar about database performance tuning. Around 200 words.

output:
**Your slowest query probably isn't the one in the bug report.**

Most teams tune the statement someone complained about. Meanwhile the real cost is a 4 ms lookup that runs 900 times per request, buried in an ORM call nobody has opened since 2023.

Join us **[DATE, TIME]** for ninety minutes on database performance tuning — the parts that survive contact with production.

What we'll cover:

- Reading an EXPLAIN plan without guessing. What a nested loop over 2M rows really costs.
- Index tradeoffs: when a covering index pays for itself, and when it just taxes every write.
- Connection pool math, and why raising your pool to 200 made latency worse.
- Spotting lock contention from the outside, before anyone hands you shell access.

**[SPEAKER NAME]** has spent [N] years keeping Postgres and MySQL fleets upright at [COMPANY], including one migration that cut p99 read latency from 1.2s to 90ms without a schema change.

Bring a slow query. The last twenty minutes are live plan review — pick one from your own system, paste it in chat, and we'll walk it. Anything we can't get to on the call gets a written answer afterward.

Free to attend. The talk is recorded; the Q&A isn't.

**[REGISTER →]**

Placeholders in brackets are yours to fill — swap the speaker credential for a real one, since a made-up number is worse than none.
